carbon_policy_signal.item: Ireland EU presidency opens six-month policy window for ETS design, carbon border rules (CBAM), and green spending acceleration before French election; risk of expedited industrial carbon pass-through and subsidy shifts H2 2026.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Accelerated ETS or CBAM phase-in could front-load industrial carbon costs into H2 2026 power pricing, raising merit-order thresholds for coal and gas dispatch and reshaping Cal+1 spreads.

freshness_caveat: Coal data stale (as of 2025-12-26, 188 days old) — 7th percentile ranking and USD 96/t price lack recent intraday signal. Clean Dark stale (2025-12-31, 183 days old); monthly +8.67 EUR/MWh cannot be trusted intraday. All other metrics current as of 2026-07-01 or 2026-07-02.
risk_flags: Storage 14.7 pp below seasonal at 49.1% full; refill pace into autumn will set Q4 power risk and gas volatility ceiling.
Clean Spark 98th percentile (68.88 EUR/MWh) vs Coal 7th percentile (96 USD/t, 188d stale); coal data age limits confidence but spread signals sustained thermal premium.
Hormuz rejection by Iran and Nord Stream indictment both escalate geopolitical premium on LNG flows; disruption would push TTF +10-15% and DE Power +8-12% within weeks.
Renewables at 21st percentile (28.89% of load, down 30.71% monthly); weak wind/solar forecast extends thermal call through summer peak.

base.summary: Renewables stay weak; storage refill steady; geopolitical premium persists but no acute disruption. TTF anchors 40–44 EUR/MWh; DE Power 150–170 EUR/MWh.

downside.summary: Renewables rebound (high wind/solar forecast); storage refill accelerates; geopolitical tensions pause. Thermal call eases; TTF and power spot recede.

upside.summary: Hormuz escalation or Iranian naval incident disrupts LNG flows; TTF premium widens. Coupled with weak renewables and refill lag, thermal push extends.

themes: Gas/power fuel-switch extended; thermal dispatch firmly in-the-money
Geopolitical tail-risk: Hormuz escalation, Nord Stream indictment, Russian fuel crisis
Storage deficit and renewable weakness sustain dispatch tension into autumn
EU policy window under Ireland presidency; climate/ETS acceleration risk
top_drivers: Clean Spark at 98th percentile driven by low renewables (21st pctile) and tight storage (49.1%, 14.7 pp below seasonal); thermal call persists.
Geopolitical escalation (Hormuz rejection, Nord Stream indictment, Russian fuel crisis) raises LNG disruption risk and EU energy security premium into H2.

German DE Power at 83rd percentile (166.6 EUR/MWh, +18.77% day) reflects intraday coal/gas mix and intra-week renewable volatility; GB Power at 17th pctile (70.92, -43.37% day) signals UK/EU spread divergence.
top_takeaway: Clean Spark at 98th percentile (68.88 EUR/MWh) amid low renewables (21st pctile) and tight storage (14.7 pp below seasonal); geopolitical risks to LNG/crude via Hormuz and Russia fuel crisis cloud H2 outlook.

watchlist.why: Iran rejection of Macron's maritime mission raises disruption probability; constrains EU LNG arb and TTF-HH spreads; watch for naval incident or shipping insurance spikes.
Ukrainian attacks forcing Russia to import gasoline; loss of export capacity tightens global crude, raises EU fuel-switching pressure and LNG scarcity risk into H2.
At 49.1% full, 14.7 pp below seasonal; August-September refill pace will determine Q4 gas volatility and power baseload costs; target 85%+ by October to avoid winter premium.
H2 2026 window before French election may accelerate ETS design, carbon border rules, green spending; timing risk for industrial carbon pass-through and power market structure shifts.
